headline: 1,521 candidates recommended for govt jobs in 47th BCS
summary: The Public Service Commission (PSC) has announced the final results, with 1,320 candidates selected for cadre posts and 201 for non-cadre positions.
details: The Public Service Commission (PSC) has recommended a total of 1,521 candidates for government jobs following the 47th Bangladesh Civil Service (BCS) examinations.
Of the successful candidates, 1,320 have been approved for cadre posts, while 201 have been nominated for non-cadre positions.
The recruitment process began with a notice on November 28, 2024, initially seeking to fill 3,487 cadre and 201 non-cadre posts.
The process saw several adjustments, including a revised circular on December 26 that reduced the application fee and lowered viva marks from 200 to 100.
For the first time, the PSC set the maximum age limit for applicants at 32. Applications were eventually accepted between December 29, 2024, and February 27, 2025.
The preliminary exam was held on September 19 across 262 institutions, with 10,644 candidates qualifying for the written stage.
Despite protests from some candidates demanding a postponement, the written exams proceeded as planned starting November 27 in eight divisional cities.
Following the written tests, 3,631 candidates passed and moved on to the viva examinations, which commenced on May 11.
caption:
1,521 candidates have been recommended for government jobs in the 47th BCS results!

The Public Service Commission (PSC) has recommended a total of 1,521 candidates for government jobs following the 47th Bangladesh Civil Service (BCS) examinations.

Of the successful candidates, 1,320 have been approved for cadre posts, while 201 have been nominated for non-cadre positions.

The recruitment process began with a notice on November 28, 2024, initially seeking to fill 3,487 cadre and 201 non-cadre posts.

The process saw several adjustments, including a revised circular on December 26 that reduced the application fee and lowered viva marks from 200 to 100.

For the first time, the PSC set the maximum age limit for applicants at 32. Applications were eventually accepted between December 29, 2024, and February 27, 2025.

The preliminary exam was held on September 19 across 262 institutions, with 10,644 candidates qualifying for the written stage.

Despite protests from some candidates demanding a postponement, the written exams proceeded as planned starting November 27 in eight divisional cities.

Following the written tests, 3,631 candidates passed and moved on to the viva examinations, which commenced on May 11.

headline: Govt appoints new divisional commissioner for Dhaka and DCs for Sylhet, Cumilla
summary: Maniruzzaman Miah is the new Dhaka divisional commissioner, while Rosy Akhter becomes the first female DC of Cumilla.
details: The government has appointed a new divisional commissioner for Dhaka and new deputy commissioners (DC) for Sylhet and Cumilla.

According to notifications from the Ministry of Public Administration, Maniruzzaman Miah, Additional Secretary of the Ministry of Housing and Public Works, has been appointed as the new divisional commissioner of Dhaka.
Reza Hasan, previously the Deputy Commissioner of Cumilla, has been transferred and appointed as the new DC of Sylhet.
Rosy Akhter, Deputy Secretary of the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism, has been appointed as the new DC of Cumilla.
Notably, Rosy Akhter becomes the first female Deputy Commissioner to serve in Cumilla.
caption:
New administrative leadership for Dhaka, Sylhet, and Cumilla. Rosy Akhter makes history as Cumilla's first female DC.

The government has appointed a new divisional commissioner for Dhaka and new deputy commissioners (DC) for Sylhet and Cumilla.

According to notifications from the Ministry of Public Administration, Maniruzzaman Miah, Additional Secretary of the Ministry of Housing and Public Works, has been appointed as the new divisional commissioner of Dhaka.

Reza Hasan, previously the Deputy Commissioner of Cumilla, has been transferred and appointed as the new DC of Sylhet.

Rosy Akhter, Deputy Secretary of the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism, has been appointed as the new DC of Cumilla.

Notably, Rosy Akhter becomes the first female Deputy Commissioner to serve in Cumilla.
